name: MaxEisen.me
shortDescription: My personal site, the one you're on: built from scratch, with a photo gallery, a live dashboard, and running and cycling training dashboards
bullets: Built from scratch in Svelte and Vite as a single-page app, on a small design system shared by every page
Hosts a photo gallery on Cloudinary with a masonry grid, lightbox, slideshow, and password-protected albums
Runs a live dashboard of Spotify, Strava, GitHub, Hacker News, and weather data through Netlify Functions
Turns Strava and Oura data into running and cycling dashboards: fitness, fatigue, recovery, and a marathon projection
Deployed on Netlify, where every push runs the test suite before it builds

name: Convoke
shortDescription: A web-based game designed to provoke abstract conversation and deep thought
bullets: A social party game built to spark abstract conversation, using OpenAI's GPT-3 API to generate a thought-provoking question each round
Includes a daily question mode for solo reflection, with answers saved locally in the browser
Built and launched in two weeks, reaching #7 on Product Hunt on launch day

name: WhatToTip
shortDescription: A web app that helps travellers save money on their next trip
bullets: A minimalist travel companion with money-saving tips for every country, built in Next.js
Generated country-specific tips at scale with OpenAI's GPT-3, driven by a custom Python script
Continuously deployed from GitHub to Vercel

name: NFTokenator
shortDescription: A Python tool that programmatically generates NFT images from layered assets
bullets: A command-line generator that produces tens of thousands of unique images in minutes from layered assets
Composites randomized trait layers with Pillow, weighted by rarities you configure
Built to be forked and extended with your own assets, traits, and validation rules

name: NuHealth
shortDescription: A web app to ease bottlenecks in Canada's public healthcare system
bullets: A dual-purpose health platform letting patients control access to their medical records while giving EMTs instant access to critical data in the field
Built with Next.js and Firebase for real-time data access and secure sign-in for first responders
Developed in under 48 hours by a team of 4 for the Publicis Sapient Aspire SPEED Hackathon, placing as a top 10 finalist

name: Eagle
shortDescription: A delivery service comparison platform to help food-lovers get the best deal
bullets: A React Native app that compares prices, delivery times, and reviews for the same restaurant across four major delivery platforms
Ideated, built, and shipped by a team of 10 that I led as product manager in QTMA
One view instead of four apps, so users can pick the best deal without checking each platform

name: Studii
shortDescription: A collaborative, all-in-one study space made for students, by students
bullets: A real-time study platform that matches students with compatible study partners and better ways to study
Built with React, Django, and MongoDB by a team of 8, with live collaboration across courses and subjects
Conceived, developed, marketed, and pitched end to end in the QTMA product incubator

name: QHacks
shortDescription: The official website for Queen's University's 2020 MLH hackathon
bullets: The official website for Queen's University's 2020 MLH-affiliated hackathon, built with React and Gatsby
The main hub for 700+ applicants, with thousands of visits through the application and pre-event period
Kept hackers informed from applications through to the event itself

name: Spotilizer
shortDescription: A customizable, data-centric Spotify music visualizer built in Python
bullets: A music visualizer that connects to a user's Spotify account and renders dynamic visuals driven by data from the Spotify Web API
Turns audio features like energy, rhythm, and danceability into real-time visuals with Python and Tkinter
Built by a team of 4 in 10 hours at MLH's 2019 Local Hack Day at Queen's University, winning 2nd place

name: Glitch
shortDescription: A minimalist, monochromatic platformer for observant players
bullets: A monochromatic Unity platformer where you toggle between two states, glitched and default, to get through each level
Puzzles reward observation and lateral thinking, and only resolve once you find the right combination of states
Built by a team of 3 as the final project for CISC 226 (Game Design) at Queen's University
